PMID:20412675.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells
PMID:20412675.standard: Information on BOA-endorsed Orthoconsent forms as the set standard for patient understanding at confirmation of consent

cycle1.result: Patients consented with standard yellow generic forms scored an average of 56.7% (knee arthroscopy) and 57.6% (total knee replacement) on questionnaires.

PMID:20412675.intervention: Patients additionally given the procedure-specific Orthoconsent form to read at home and sign on the morning of surgery.

cycle2.result: Average scores rose to 80.5% (knee arthroscopy) and 81.6% (total knee replacement).

PMID:20412675.other_findings: 100 knee arthroscopy and 60 total knee replacement patients took part in total; questionnaires had 26 (KA) or 35 (TKR) questions.

PMID:26045146.setting: Orthopaedic Unit, Alice Springs Hospital (rural hospital)

cycle1.result: 114 hand infection admissions, 87 (76%) in Indigenous patients; MRSA rate 24.6%; Indigenous patients 9.52 times more likely to be re-admitted (P = 0.038).

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:26045146.other_findings: Indigenous and older patients had longer admissions; MRSA was associated with smoking and substance abuse.

EPMC:PPR:PPR818934.setting: Orthogeriatric unit (experimental group) with a conventional orthopaedic unit as control
EPMC:PPR:PPR818934.standard: Receipt of acetaminophen 3 g/day during the three postoperative days, and nurses' adherence to medical prescriptions

cycle1.result: 16% of patients in the experimental group received 3 g/day of acetaminophen postoperatively before the intervention.

EPMC:PPR:PPR818934.intervention: Audit and feedback intervention built with nurses.

cycle2.result: 60% received 3 g/day of acetaminophen after the intervention; likelihood of receiving 3 g/day and prescription adherence significantly increased versus control.

EPMC:PPR:PPR818934.other_findings: 398 patients in total (mean age 89 years); functional status at discharge was better and length of stay shorter after the intervention.

PMID:26802946.setting: Departments of Radiology and Orthopaedic Surgery, Royal Devon and Exeter Hospital

cycle1.result: Significant improvement in pain at rest, on activity and function in both insertional and non-insertional groups over two years.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:26802946.other_findings: Satisfaction scores improved significantly in the non-insertional group but not the insertional group.

PMID:39937317.setting: Quality improvement collaborative across 19 hospitals in Flanders
PMID:39937317.standard: Adherence to 23 quality indicators for geriatric hip fracture care

cycle1.result: Lowest adherence: nerve blocks 8.0%, steroids 9.7%, tranexamic acid 22.2%.

PMID:39937317.intervention: Anonymous benchmarking fed back to centres and three educative sessions on specific topics.

cycle2.result: Nerve blocks 25.4%, steroids 26.4%, tranexamic acid 30.7% (significant improvement).

PMID:39937317.other_findings: 1044 patients were included across both retrospective audits.

PMID:27255575.topic: Gentamicin prophylaxis for urinary catheter manipulation
PMID:27255575.setting: Antimicrobial stewardship team, 500-bed tertiary regional hospital (Wollongong Hospital)
PMID:27255575.standard: Australian Therapeutic Guidelines: Antibiotic (no recognised indication for gentamicin IDC prophylaxis)

cycle1.result: Gentamicin given for IDC insertion in 59/137 (42%) operations.

PMID:27255575.intervention: Results presented to surgeons, literature review, consensus to discontinue gentamicin IDC prophylaxis, with weekly feedback to the Head of Orthopaedics.

cycle2.result: Gentamicin for IDC insertion fell to 4/205 (2%).

PMID:27255575.other_findings: Regular rolling audits and timely feedback helped sustain the change.

PMID:33143866.topic: National Hip Fracture Database data accuracy
PMID:33143866.setting: Multi-centre quality improvement study (hip arthroplasty episodes recorded in the NHFD)
PMID:33143866.standard: Accuracy of NHFD entries for operation, implant polarity and cementation

cycle1.result: Inaccuracies in 20.5% of 3972 data entries.

PMID:33143866.intervention: Introduction of a hip fracture clinical data administrator in each centre.

cycle2.result: Inaccuracies reduced to 5.2% of 559 data entries.

PMID:33143866.other_findings: Authors advise caution when using NHFD data for research and audit.

PMID:22041145.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Princess Royal Hospital, Haywards Heath

cycle1.result: PACU admissions 22%, mortality 6.1%, HDU length of stay 2.1 days, ICU unplanned admissions 1.3%, ICU length of stay 2.3 days.

PMID:22041145.intervention: Multidisciplinary anaesthetic-led preoperative assessment clinic started in April 2006.

cycle2.result: PACU admissions 10%, mortality 1.2% (p = 0.001); HDU length of stay 1.6 days, ICU unplanned admissions 0.4%, ICU length of stay 1.9 days (p = 0.01).

PMID:22041145.other_findings: Estimated cost savings of nearly £50,000 in the second period.

PMID:41418243.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedics, Northwest General Hospital and Research Centre, Peshawar
PMID:41418243.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England operation note guidelines (19 parameters)

cycle1.result: 64 notes (45 (70%) typewritten); 64 (100%) compliant for surgeon name, operative procedure, diagnosis and post-op instructions.

PMID:41418243.intervention: Findings presented in ward meetings with surgeons and educational workshops arranged.

cycle2.result: Average improvement of 40 (31.1%), with 17 of 19 categories improving.

PMID:41418243.other_findings: 128 notes reviewed in total; 50 (78%) of post-intervention notes were typewritten.

PMID:35509294.setting: East Sussex Healthcare Trust, elective shoulder surgery

cycle1.result: Grade 1 (complete agreement) 87.0% (n = 47), Grade 2 9.3% (n = 5), Grade 3 3.7% (n = 2); 96% closely correlated with surgical findings.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:35509294.other_findings: Ultrasound was more accurate than MRI for full-thickness rotator cuff tears but unreliable in patients with BMI ≥ 35.

EPMC:PMC:PMC9567124.topic: Falls prevention and management in inpatients
EPMC:PMC:PMC9567124.setting: Woodlands Hospital, inpatient old age psychiatric unit
EPMC:PMC:PMC9567124.standard: NICE guidelines on the management of falls in older people

cycle1.result: 100% had individualised interventions; 97.3% had falls risk assessment on admission; 60.3% checked for signs of fracture; 78.3% had physical examination within 12 hours; 75% had neurological observations.

cycle2.result: not reported

EPMC:PMC:PMC9567124.other_findings: Weekly MDT falls risk review, fracture checks and neurological examination need improvement; re-audit planned for September 2021.

PMID:32554686.setting: GP practice with a population of 14,000

cycle1.result: 75% of patients followed the local guidelines pathway.

cycle2.result: 81% of patients followed the local guidelines pathway.

PMID:32554686.other_findings: Practice clinical system searches identified uncoded or untreated patients with osteoporosis or fragility fracture.

PMID:12793549.topic: Blood transfusion in lower limb arthroplasty
PMID:12793549.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Royal Preston Hospital

cycle1.result: 66% transfused at least one unit (58% of knees, 73% of hips); mean transfusion requirement given as 13 units per patient (1.1 knees, 1.5 hips).

PMID:12793549.intervention: New transfusion protocol based on maximum allowable blood loss, colloid replacement, bedside haematocrit and transfusion thresholds, with Hb checks on days 1-3.

cycle2.result: 24% required blood (11% of knees, 34% of hips); mean 0.56 units per patient (0.26 knees, 0.79 hips).

PMID:12793549.other_findings: Prospective audits of 38 knees and 41 hips, then 35 knees and 47 hips.

PMID:17938779.topic: Hip fracture data quality: audit versus register data
PMID:17938779.setting: Kuusankoski Regional Hospital with Finnish Health Care Register and Causes of Death Register

cycle1.result: Register accuracy of easily measurable variables at least 95%; agreement with audit data 86.3% for detailed hip fracture diagnosis; polyserial correlation 0.68 for functional dependency.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:17938779.other_findings: Register data lack clinical detail but outperform prospective data for inpatient care history.

PMID:21056162.topic: Red flag documentation in low back pain
PMID:21056162.setting: 14 NHS health boards in Scotland plus two private provider sites (physiotherapy services)
PMID:21056162.standard: Evidence- and consensus-based guideline recommendations on red flag assessment in low back pain

cycle1.result: Documentation of all red flags 33% (n=709); cauda equina syndrome 60% (n=1288).

PMID:21056162.intervention: Improvement phase between cycles (details not given in the abstract).

cycle2.result: Documentation of all red flags 65% (n=1396); cauda equina syndrome 84% (n=1804).

PMID:21056162.other_findings: Data from 2147 patients; only two regions documented all cauda equina components 100%, and one in five patients still did not receive optimal management.

PMID:18689336.setting: Division of Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery, Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital

cycle1.result: 95 condylar fractures; 73.8% from interpersonal violence; 73 (87%) unilateral; Type I 31%, Type II 26%, Type III 25%.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:18689336.other_findings: Prolonged intermaxillary fixation, no training elastics, no physiotherapy and poor compliance increased hypomobility risk.

PMID:17132315.setting: Orthopaedic outpatients, Princess Royal Hospital, Haywards Heath
PMID:17132315.standard: Independent management of 85% of patients by ESPs; no re-referral with the same problem; patient satisfaction 89%

cycle1.result: 82/150 (55%) managed independently; 4/150 (3%) re-referred by GPs; 97/126 (77%) satisfied.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:17132315.other_findings: Consultant review was needed for 81% of shoulder, 34% of knee and 11% of back cases.

PMID:17132318.setting: Fracture clinic, Department of Orthopaedics, Frimley Park Hospital

cycle1.result: 84% thought a 'fracture' and a 'break' differ; 68% believed a 'break' is worse.

PMID:17132318.intervention: Patient information leaflet on fractures/broken bones introduced.

cycle2.result: 67% thought there was a difference; 65% believed a 'break' is worse.

PMID:17132318.other_findings: Only 21% read the leaflet and 69% of those still believed there was a difference.

cycle1.result: Readmission rate 12.1% (47/346) in children with fractures; 16% loss of position after closed reduction; 24% of internal fixations were salvage procedures.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:9422873.other_findings: Femoral fractures had prolonged stays due to wide variation in treatment method.

PMID:35938506.setting: Multicentre national collaborative audit across NHS trusts
PMID:35938506.standard: National orthopaedic society recommendations on PROMs collection

cycle1.result: PROMs collected for 83.3% of hip and 80.6% of knee replacements; 69% (221/318) used paper as primary collection method; variation outside incentivised programmes failed to meet the audit standard.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:35938506.other_findings: 63 trusts enrolled, 38 (60%) completed; 21 procedures were assessed.

PMID:20375829.topic: Multimodal oral analgesia after spine surgery
PMID:20375829.setting: Department of Neurosurgery, University of Wisconsin Hospital and Clinics

cycle1.result: Historical control group received conventional IV PCA.

PMID:20375829.intervention: Perioperative oral multimodal analgesia regimen (extended-release oxycodone, gabapentin, acetaminophen, dolasetron, as-needed oral oxycodone).

cycle2.result: Significantly less opioid consumption with the multimodal regimen (p value not given in abstract).

PMID:20375829.other_findings: Outcomes measured over the first 24 hours by patient surveys and chart audit.

PMID:18765028.topic: Stable ankle fracture management in functional brace
PMID:18765028.setting: A&E and orthopaedic departments, North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Trust
PMID:18765028.standard: Local evidence-based guidelines for diagnosis, functional brace treatment and follow-up of stable ankle fractures

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:18765028.intervention: Guidelines with diagnostic criteria, brace management protocol and outpatient follow-up algorithm widely distributed, with persistent education of colleagues.

cycle2.result: 91% managed in a functional brace; mean outpatient appointments, weeks to discharge and repeat radiographs fell significantly.

PMID:18765028.other_findings: A previous audit had shown 60% of stable fractures could be treated in a brace; the change produced significant cost savings.

PMID:40467445.setting: Emergency department, Sunshine Coast University Hospital

cycle1.result: Helmet non-compliance 42%; doubling 12%; 36% exceeded 25 km/hr; fractures 37%; CT 18%; 11% life-threatening or potentially life-threatening injuries.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:40467445.other_findings: Median age 14 years, 71% male; falls caused 78% of crashes.

PMID:42061883.topic: Periprosthetic femur fracture epidemiology and outcomes
PMID:42061883.setting: 16 centres, Scottish National Audit of Periprosthetic Femur Fractures with Scottish Hip Fracture Audit data

cycle1.result: 328 PFFs, mean age 79 years, 66% female; PFF patients were less frail than native hip fracture patients (median CFS 4 vs 5).

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:42061883.other_findings: PFFs were associated with increased mortality risk and functional decline; most are likely missed in arthroplasty registries.

PMID:31498659.topic: Best practice tariff compliance for hip and knee replacement
PMID:31498659.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery Department, Chelsea and Westminster Hospital
PMID:31498659.standard: Best practice tariff criteria: NJR compliance at least 85%, NJR unknown consent below 15%, PROMs participation ≥50%, average health gain not significantly below national average

cycle1.result: PROMs participation rate 31% due to a systematic error in submitting preoperative PROM scores.

PMID:31498659.intervention: PROM data resubmitted under the trust's correct organisation data service code.

cycle2.result: PROMs compliance 90% and all criteria satisfied.

PMID:31498659.other_findings: This resulted in over £450,000 of additional reimbursement to the trust.

PMID:33618957.setting: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences

cycle1.result: Mean time in each chart before arthroplasty 76.8 (SD 47.8) minutes; surgeon 7.9, registered nurses 46.7, physician extenders 10.8, LPNs and technicians 9.8 minutes.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:34311818.setting: West Palm Beach Veterans Affairs Medical Center (acute care, subacute rehabilitation and outpatients)
PMID:34311818.standard: American Pain Society guideline recommendations for perioperative multimodal analgesia (at least two medication classes)

cycle1.result: Perioperative multimodal analgesia used in 85%; 87% discharged on multimodal analgesia.

PMID:34311818.intervention: Evidence-based multimodal perioperative quick-order menu developed (no re-audit reported).

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:34311818.other_findings: 67% response rate to the internal ERAS protocol audit from the orthopaedic team.

PMID:23351497.topic: Operating theatre waste in knee arthroplasty
PMID:23351497.setting: London Health Sciences Centre, single surgeon

cycle1.result: Average surgical waste 13.3 kg per TKA: 8.6 kg (64.5%) normal solid waste, 2.5 kg (19.2%) biohazard, 1.6 kg (12.1%) blue sterile wrap, 0.3 kg (2.2%) recyclables, 0.3 kg (2.2%) sharps.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:23351497.other_findings: Estimated landfill waste from 47 429 Canadian TKAs in 2008-2009 was 407 889 kg and 15 272 m3.

PMID:32930608.setting: Institute of Neurological Sciences, Queen Elizabeth University Hospital, Glasgow
PMID:32930608.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England operation note guidelines

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:32930608.intervention: Results presented to the department orally and as posters in clinical areas.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:32930608.other_findings: Estimated blood loss remained recorded less often in both cycles; registrars rated missing sub-domains as least important.

PMID:16133648.standard: Fracture protocol based on Australian Fracture Prevention Summit recommendations for in-hospital calcium, vitamin D, SERMs and bisphosphonates

cycle1.result: In-hospital prescription: any treatment 36%, calcium 26%, vitamin D 29%, oral bisphosphonates 5%, SERMs 1%.

cycle2.result: Any treatment 58%, calcium 51%, vitamin D 48%, oral bisphosphonates 24% (all P <0.01); SERMs 1% (P =0.70).

PMID:16133648.other_findings: In-hospital death and dementia reduced the likelihood of starting treatment.

PMID:40028186.topic: Operating theatre waste in knee arthroplasty
PMID:40028186.setting: Hospital operating room and ambulatory surgery center, Springfield, Illinois

cycle1.result: Total waste mass 17.3 kg (hospital) vs 14.0 kg (ASC), p = 0.0028; volume 305,866 cm3 vs 260,052 cm3, p = 0.2494.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:40028186.other_findings: Sterile waste was the largest contributor in both settings.

PMID:2390307.setting: Lincoln County Hospital and GP practices in its catchment

cycle1.result: Total referral rate 9.6 referrals/100 patients/year, ranging from 2.8 to 17.6 between practices.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:2390307.other_findings: A working group of orthopaedic surgeons and GPs met to draw up agreed referral protocols.

PMID:20615303.setting: Adult Lower Extremity Reconstruction, Mount Sinai Hospital, Toronto
PMID:20615303.standard: Evidence-based guidelines recommending VTE prophylaxis for 4 weeks after hip arthroplasty

cycle1.result: Enoxaparin 40 mg once daily: mean duration of prophylaxis 5.4 days.

PMID:20615303.intervention: Switch to oral rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily.

cycle2.result: Rivaroxaban: mean duration of prophylaxis 35 days.

PMID:20615303.other_findings: International survey: 4 of 39 (10.2%) units prescribing LMWH did so for at least 4 weeks.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524515.standard: BOAST 11 standards for supracondylar humeral fractures

cycle1.result: not reported

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524515.intervention: Information booklet created and distributed to all doctors in the department.

cycle2.result: Compliance improved in five BOAST 11 domains: neurovascular assessment documented in clerking improved by 28%; 2 mm k-wire use documented improved by 23%; operation within 24 hours regressed.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8524515.other_findings: Re-audit took place during the COVID-19 pandemic.

PMID:30388022.topic: ACL reconstruction return to play in elite sport
PMID:30388022.setting: Australian Football League player injury registry

cycle1.result: Return to play 77% (121 of 158); subsequent ACL injury 30% (48 of 158).

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:30388022.other_findings: Greater preinjury experience and earlier draft selection were associated with higher return to play.

PMID:31230423.setting: Orthopaedic unit, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne (tertiary metropolitan hospital)

cycle1.result: 82.2% (n = 231) discharged on opioids; 71.4% discharged on combination opioids.

PMID:31230423.intervention: Expert Advisory Group oversight of opioid prescribing, a prescription opioid guideline and a series of education sessions.

cycle2.result: 79.6% (n = 230) discharged on opioids; combination opioids fell to 45.7%.

PMID:31230423.other_findings: A high proportion of patients were still discharged on opioids.

PMID:24292423.setting: Department of Radiology, Cumberland Infirmary, Carlisle
PMID:24292423.standard: New local guidelines for scaphoid injury diagnostics (early MRI after inconclusive initial radiograph)

cycle1.result: Follow-up radiographs detected 1/23 (4%) fractures; bone scan 6/41 (15%); MRI 4/13 (31%); mean time from initial radiograph to MRI 36 days.

PMID:24292423.intervention: New local guidelines introduced with early MRI replacing follow-up radiographs and bone scans.

cycle2.result: 7 of 77 (9%) diagnosed with scaphoid fracture; mean time to MRI 14 days.

PMID:31036485.setting: Regional spinal service, Western General Hospital, Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Lower limb neurology, urinary function and saddle sensation were almost universally documented; sexual function poorly documented.

PMID:31036485.intervention: Results presented locally to increase awareness.

cycle2.result: Significant increase in documentation of certain features (p value not given in abstract); sexual function still poorly documented.

PMID:31036485.other_findings: 120 patients across both periods; 25 had radiological cauda equina compression.

PMID:29540450.setting: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, London (tertiary spinal surgery centre)
PMID:29540450.standard: Royal College of Surgeons documentation guidelines (GMC/NICE)

cycle1.result: not reported

PMID:29540450.intervention: Standardised clerking pro forma for surgical spinal patients.

cycle2.result: Pro forma significantly improved documentation in admission clerking (no figures given in abstract).

PMID:29540450.other_findings: Further work is needed for widespread use of the pro forma.

PMID:30306703.setting: Orthopaedic and neurosurgical wards, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne

cycle1.result: About 82% discharged on opioids; combination opioids in 71.4% (orthopaedic) and 73.8% (neurosurgical); only 6.9% and 11.5% of discharge summaries referred to opioid management.

cycle2.result: not reported

PMID:30306703.other_findings: Around 65% of those discharged on opioids were opioid naive on admission.
